title: Cloud KMS master-key wrap spike (enc:v2 envelope)
story: As a carrier security officer I want the master key wrapped by Cloud KMS so that no plaintext master key sits on disk.
valueDrivers: No plaintext master key at rest
Key rotation and audit through KMS
requirements: ADR-001 zero dependencies; global fetch only
acceptance: src/core/keywrap.mjs exports a Kms port contract (wrapKey(plaintextDek) and unwrapKey(wrapped, keyId) async) with createFakeKms() for tests, createCloudKmsRest({tokenProvider, keyName, fetch}) building Cloud KMS REST encrypt/decrypt calls, and encryptV2/decryptV2 (or equivalent) producing an envelope string starting with enc:v2: that carries the KMS key id, the KMS-wrapped DEK and AES-256-GCM ciphertext (iv, tag) with the key id and version bound as AAD.

keywrap.test.mjs passes: round-trip via fake KMS; fresh random DEK and IV per value; tamper of ciphertext, wrapped DEK or key id fails; wrong key id fails; enc:v1 values produced by the existing crypto.mjs still decrypt through a dispatch function decryptAny(value) that routes v1 to the existing crypto.mjs export and v2 to the KMS path; plaintext not present in envelope; REST request shape tested with fake fetch and fake token provider.
crypto.mjs untouched (git diff clean) and used only by import; no re-encryption or migration code; no key material or secrets committed.

Token comes from src/core/gcp-auth.mjs createTokenProvider (owned by S5-PLT-02) or an injected tokenProvider parameter; tests use only fakes (inject {getToken}), so this ticket does not depend on the file existing. No network in tests.

architecture/spikes/kms-keywrap.md covers: envelope format spec, DEK caching and per-tenant key id option, rotation (new key version for new writes, old still unwrap), failure modes and fail-closed behaviour, IAM roles (cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter), cost and latency notes, and a documented live-check command for the orchestrator (not under tests/).
brief: Spike, small proof, no migration. Read src/core/crypto.mjs and architecture/data-protection.md to learn the exact enc:v1 format and its exported functions; do not edit crypto.mjs. Envelope proposal (document it): enc:v2:<keyIdB64url>:<wrappedDekB64url>:<ivB64url>:<tagB64url>:<ctB64url>. Encrypt: random 32-byte DEK, AES-256-GCM with random 12-byte IV, AAD = 'enc:v2|' + keyId; wrap DEK via kms.wrapKey; zero the DEK buffer after use (buffer.fill(0)). Decrypt: parse strictly, unwrapKey(wrapped, keyId), verify GCM tag. Cloud KMS REST: POST https://cloudkms.googleapis.com/v1/{keyName}:encrypt body {plaintext: base64} returns {ciphertext, name}; :decrypt body {ciphertext} returns {plaintext}. keyName looks like projects/example-project/locations/global/keyRings/example/cryptoKeys/master (synthetic). The returned name on encrypt includes cryptoKeyVersions; store the base key name as key id. Fake KMS: wrap with an in-memory AES-GCM key and support multiple key ids/versions to test rotation. Import the token provider from ./gcp-auth.mjs ONLY via a parameter (do not import statically, since S5-PLT-02 may land at the same time); default usage documented in the spike. decryptAny(value, {v1Decrypt, kms}) takes v1 decrypter as a parameter to keep it testable, with a test that wires the real crypto.mjs export. Error messages must not include plaintext or key bytes.

verdicts.reason: All criteria met; 13/13 keywrap tests pass, e2e/security matches baseline (372 pass, 0 fail), crypto.mjs untouched, fakes only
